title: Automated Compliance Artifact Indexer for Multi-Jurisdictional Retention
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Problem: Customers in regulated industries require auditable, exportable evidence bundles that prove configuration, access events, and data residency/retention behavior across regions. Today our retention metadata is scattered (S3 buckets, DB flags, policy TTLs) and evidence collection is manual for audits. This creates long lead times for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 audits and risk of missed artifacts when customers change regions or opt into Dedicated/Private deployments.

Goal: Build an indexer service + lightweight artifact manifest that (1) continuously indexes compliance-relevant artifacts and their retention metadata across environments, (2) provides a queryable API for auditors and the Console, and (3) supports automated bundle generation (signed, hashed, with provenance) for export and attestation. The feature must respect region boundaries, honor retention TTLs, and integrate with the existing evidence collector pipeline.

Out of scope: full e-discovery UI, long-term storage of raw logs beyond configured retention, and legal hold flows (will be a follow-up).

Success metrics: reduce manual evidence collection time for auditors by >= 80%, enable single-click export of SOC 2 artifact bundles for 90% of audit playbooks, and end-to-end proof-of-presence check for artifacts across regions with < 1% false negatives.
acceptance_criteria: Indexer collects metadata for artifacts (config snapshots, ACLs, audit logs, encryption key rotations) from hosted, dedicated, and private control planes with region labels attached.
Query API supports filters: control ID (SOC2/ISO mapping), region, artifact type, time range, and retention state (active/expired/archived).
Console UI surface shows per-control artifact counts and retention compliance status; each artifact has a stable manifest ID and a SHA256 fingerprint.
Exportable evidence bundle contains a signed manifest.json, compressed artifacts (or pointers for large logs), and a provenance header listing collector versions and timestamps.
Retention enforcement report demonstrates artifacts subject to retention TTLs and indicates any policy mismatches detected during indexing.
Automated smoke test replicates an audit playbook and verifies presence of expected artifacts (unit tests + e2e harness).
Feature respects data-residency constraints: artifacts ingested from a region remain indexed under that region and bundles created for a jurisdiction contain only allowed artifacts.
implementation_notes: Design a compact manifest spec: {manifest_id, artifact_id, artifact_type, sha256, size_bytes, region, retention_policy_id, created_ts, collector_version}. (Will be expressed in PRD; here as guidelines).

Indexer components: collector adapters (S3 metadata crawler, control-plane snapshotter, audit-log sampler), central indexer service (append-only store of manifest records), and query API with paginated endpoints.
Collectors must publish collector_version and a deterministic manifest_id to aid reproducible bundles and allow auditors to validate provenance.

Retention model: canonical retention policy records stored in ConfigDB (ENG to own), indexer evaluates artifact TTLs relative to policy and emits compliance alerts if artifact outlives policy or lacks region tag.
Security: manifests are signed using a service key stored in KMS; implement rotating signing keys and include key ID in manifest header.
Privacy: for Private deployments, indexer runs in customer VPC and emits only metadata pointers to control plane; support local bundle generation to avoid cross-jurisdiction transfers.
Console UX: per-control timeline and an 'audit bundle' CTA that triggers bundle generation and posts status updates to the audit job log.
Backward compatibility: indexer will import existing evidence buckets using a one-time migration job; add a migration flag to prevent double-counting.
Performance: indexer must sustain 1000 artifact events/minute for large tenants; design for batching and backpressure to avoid DB hotspots.
Rollout: start with hosted dataset pilot, then enable Dedicated customers by opt-in, finally Private via on-prem agent release.
rollout_plan: Week 0-2: API & manifest spec review with Security, Legal, and Research. Create RFC and get sign-off.
Week 3-5: Build collector adapters (S3 crawler, control-plane snapshot endpoint). Start internal pilot on synthetic tenant.
Week 6: Console integration: UI for per-control artifact list and audit bundle CTA in feature-flagged mode.
Week 7: Small hosted beta with 3 customers (one mid-market SaaS, one enterprise, 1 Dedicated). Collect feedback and compliance edge-cases.
Week 8-9: Fixes, finalize signing key rotation, and run security review. Prepare documentation and audit playbook examples.
Week 10: GA rollout behind tenant-level opt-in; publish docs and sample manifests for auditors.
Post-GA: telemetry dashboard for evidence-index coverage, false-negative rate, and bundle generation latency; follow-on to support legal-hold flows.

qa_checks: Unit tests for manifest serialization/deserialization and signature verification.
Integration tests ingesting sample artifacts from 3 regions and verifying correct region-tagging in index.
E2E audit-playbook runner that attempts to export bundle and validate all SHA256 fingerprints.
Load test showing indexer sustaining expected artifact ingestion rate with < 5s indexing latency under load.
risk_mitigation: If retention policy conflicts are detected, indexer emits a high-priority alert and creates a remediation ticket for infra to reconcile policy sources.
Collector adapters run in read-only mode; no automatic deletion of artifacts — prevents accidental data loss. Deletion remains controlled by retention enforcement subsystem with explicit approvals.
Private installs: provide a local-only bundle generator to ensure no cross-border transfer of raw artifacts.
Key compromise plan: rotate service signing keys, publish revocation list in bundle header, and re-sign manifests where required.
